rule: Code outside a method body: the caller is its location. Field/val initializer → `Type#field`; ... `static {}` block → `Type#<clinit>`. Non-lazy initializers also get an `implicit` edge from `<clinit>`/`<init>`; lazy ones do not. ... `implicit`: ... `Type#<clinit>` → `Type#field` (static initializer), `Type#<init>` → `Type#field` (instance field initializer). Line = the field's line.
notes: call_type convention (SPEC names the six call_types but does not define direct vs method): a call with no written receiver is direct; a call with a written receiver (obj., this., super., a type name) is method; new/super(...)/this(...) are constructor. Static field DEFAULT gets the implicit edge from <clinit>; instance fields keys/loader from <init> (Settings has no written constructor; its implicit one runs the initializers). SPEC does not state a confidence for implicit edges; high is used because both ends are defined in the scanned source (Confidence tiers: high). `new Settings()` is high: the class is in the scan (see 02 notes). `keys` is declared `List<String>`, so List#size (declared type, not ArrayList), medium, qualified through `import java.util.List`.
